definition: a Surface Form is one spelling of a word. the Lexicon contains every Surface Form of the language. the Lexicon gives one Form Tag to every Surface Form.
a Lemma is one entry of the Seed. a Lemma is the base spelling of a word. Lexgen expands every Lemma into the Surface Forms of the Lemma.
a Category is the class of a Lemma. people choose one Category for every Lemma. the Category decides the Surface Forms of the Lemma.
a Form Tag names the class of one Surface Form. every Surface Form has one Form Tag. the Form Tag comes from the Category of the Lemma.
the Seed is the file "seed/seed.json". people edit the Seed. every entry of the Seed names one Lemma. the entry names the Category of the Lemma. Lexgen builds the Lexicon from the Seed.
the Lexicon is the file "lexicon.tsv". Lexgen writes the Lexicon from the Seed. the Lexicon contains every Surface Form and contains every Redirect. people do not edit the Lexicon.
a Paradigm contains every Surface Form of one Lemma. Lexgen builds the Paradigm of a Lemma from the Category of the Lemma.
if 2 Lemmas produce one Surface Form, then the Surface Form is a Collision. if one Surface Form has 2 Form Tags, then the Surface Form is a Collision. Lexgen rejects every Collision.
a Redirect names a replacement for a Rejected Sense of a word. the Linter shows the Redirect to the writer.
the maintainers can waive the Redirect of a Rejected Sense. the Waiver records the choice.

if the Lexicon contains every word of a sentence, then the Coverage counts the sentence. the Coverage is a share of the corpus. the Coverage is a proxy. the Coverage does not measure the quality of the Redirects.
if the Linter does not parse a sentence, then the sentence is a Rejection. a Rejection is a Ban or is a Gap. the Linter must explain every Rejection.
a Ban is a Rejection of an ambiguous structure. the Ban is permanent. the writer changes the sentence. the Linter explains the Ban.
a Translation Pair has an original sentence and has a translation. the Linter must parse the translation. the translation must keep every claim of the original sentence.

a translation can drop the politeness of the original sentence. a translation can drop the emphasis of the original sentence. the Translation Pair must declare every loss. a Declared Loss is a declaration of a loss. a translation cannot drop a claim.
the Linter checks a sentence. the Linter parses the sentence or explains the Rejection. the Linter names the kind of a Rejection.
the Grammar defines every Sentence Shape of the language. the Grammar gives one Parse to every sentence.
a Sentence Shape is a structure of a sentence. the Grammar defines every Sentence Shape. every sentence of the language uses one Sentence Shape.
a Parse is one structure of a sentence. every sentence of the language has one Parse.
an Anaphoric Pronoun refers to a noun of a prior sentence. the reader must find the noun. the language bans every Anaphoric Pronoun. the writer repeats the noun.
an Indexical Pronoun refers to the writer or refers to the reader. the pronoun "i" is an Indexical Pronoun. the pronoun "you" is an Indexical Pronoun. the language allows Indexical Pronouns.
a Discourse Layer resolves the referent of an Anaphoric Pronoun. the language does not have a Discourse Layer.
if a reader cannot find the referent of a pronoun, then the sentence has a Reference Ambiguity. the design of the language removes every Reference Ambiguity.
a Function Word is a word of a Closed Class. a Function Word has one meaning. the Grammar gives one meaning to every Function Word.
Minglish is the language of the project. every sentence of Minglish has one Parse.
Lexgen is a tool. Lexgen builds the Lexicon from the Seed. Lexgen rejects every Collision.
Triage is a tool. Triage measures the Coverage of the Lexicon.
WordNet is a database. WordNet attests the senses of the words.
people curate the Seed. people choose every Lemma.
the Linter lints a sentence. the Linter checks the words and checks the structure.
the Linter parses a sentence. the Linter finds the Parse of the sentence.
the maintainers waive the Redirect of a Rejected Sense. the Waiver records the choice.
the data attests the words. if the data does not attest a Surface Form, then Lexgen rejects the Surface Form.
an anaphoric word refers to a noun of a prior sentence.
an indexical word refers to the writer or refers to the reader.
a transitive verb needs an object.
an intransitive verb does not need an object.
a Rejected Sense is a sense of a word. the Seed does not enable the Rejected Sense. the Linter rejects the Rejected Sense. a Rejected Sense has a Redirect or has a Waiver.
a Gap is a Rejection of a good sentence. the language cannot say the sentence. the maintainers fix a Gap with a decision.
a Closed Class contains Function Words. a Closed Class does not grow. people cannot add a word to a Closed Class.

an Enumeration is a block. the block has a statement. the block has a list of the items. the statement ends with a colon. every item names one thing. the items enumerate the last Noun Phrase of the statement.
a Noun Phrase names one thing. a Noun Phrase has a noun or is a quoted word.
a Copula is the word "is" or is the word "are". a Copula links the subject of a sentence to a Complement. a Copula does not take an object.
a Complement follows a Copula. a Complement is an adjective or is a Noun Phrase. a Complement is not a Participle.
a Participle is a Surface Form of a verb. a Complement is not a Participle. if a Participle follows a noun, then the sentence has a Reduced Relative.
a Passive drops the doer of a verb. the sentence "the file is stored" is a Passive. the language bans every Passive.
a Progressive has a Copula. a Progressive has a Participle. the sentence "the agent is running" is a Progressive. the language bans every Progressive.
the Tense of a verb marks the time of the action. the language has the present Tense. the language has the past Tense.
if a Participle follows a noun, then the Noun Phrase is a Reduced Relative. the sentence "the file stored in the database fails" has a Reduced Relative. the language bans every Reduced Relative.
a Coordination joins 2 phrases with a conjunction. the 2 phrases have one Category. the language has 2 conjunctions.
a Conjunct is one phrase of a Coordination. every Conjunct carries the Modifiers of the Conjunct.
a Modifier is an adjective or is a Prepositional Phrase. a Modifier describes one Noun Phrase. a Modifier does not cover a Coordination.
a Prepositional Phrase has a preposition. a Prepositional Phrase has a Noun Phrase. a Prepositional Phrase attaches to a verb or attaches to a noun.
a Prohibition is a command. a Prohibition has the phrase "do not". the sentence "do not delete the file" is a Prohibition. a Prohibition is a Sentence Shape of the language.
a Negation is a statement. a Negation has the word "not". the word "not" changes the truth of the verb. the language uses "does not" for a verb and uses "is not" for a Copula.

an Auxiliary is a Function Word. an Auxiliary helps a verb. the word "do" is an Auxiliary. the language uses an Auxiliary in a Negation. the language uses an Auxiliary in a Prohibition. the language does not use an Auxiliary in a plain statement.
a Constituent is one part of a sentence. a Noun Phrase is a Constituent. a Prepositional Phrase is a Constituent.
if a reader cannot tell the Constituent of a word, then the sentence has a Scope Ambiguity. the word "not" causes a Scope Ambiguity in English.

the Cognitive Load of a sentence is the work of the reader. the Open Dependencies predict the Cognitive Load. the Dependency Length predicts the Cognitive Load. the Embedding Depth predicts the Cognitive Load.
an Open Dependency is a relation. the relation links 2 words of a sentence. the reader holds an Open Dependency in the memory. the comfortable bound is 4 Open Dependencies.
the Dependency Length is a distance. the distance separates the 2 words of one relation. a long Dependency Length costs the reader.
the Embedding Depth counts the clauses inside a clause. a deep embedding costs the reader.
the Context Need of a sentence is the prior text of the sentence. a reader needs the prior text. a good sentence has a small Context Need.
a Language Model is a program. a Language Model reads a text and writes a text. a Language Model has a small memory.
a Conditional is a Sentence Shape. a Conditional has a condition and has a consequent. the word "if" opens the condition. the word "then" opens the consequent.
English is the language of the original texts. Minglish is a subset of English.
a Bare Plural is a plural noun. a Bare Plural does not have a determiner. a Bare Plural names a kind. the sentence "machines find collisions" has a Bare Plural.
a Noun Preposition attaches to the prior noun. the word "of" is the Noun Preposition. the language has one Noun Preposition.
a Verb Preposition attaches to the verb of the clause. the word "in" is a Verb Preposition. a clause has one Verb Preposition.
a Propositional Loss changes a claim of the original sentence. a Propositional Loss drops a quantifier or drops a doer. a Translation Pair cannot have a Propositional Loss.
a Register Loss drops the politeness of the original sentence or drops the emphasis of the original sentence. a Translation Pair declares every Register Loss.
a Structure Loss changes the order of the information. a Passive of the original sentence causes a Structure Loss. a Translation Pair declares every Structure Loss.
the Dogfood is a test of the language. the maintainers lint the documents of the project. the Dogfood finds the Gaps of the language.
a Compound has 2 nouns. a determiner does not separate the 2 nouns. the phrase "discourse layer" is a Compound. the language bans every Compound. a writer uses a term or uses a paraphrase.
the First Token of a sentence announces the Sentence Shape. the word "if" is the First Token of a Conditional. every Sentence Shape has a distinct First Token.
the Head Noun of a Compound is the last noun of the Compound. the Head Noun names the kind of the thing.
a Name is one token. a Name is a capitalized word or is a quoted span. a Name does not inflect. the writer repeats a Name.
an Imperative is a Sentence Shape. a verb opens an Imperative. the sentence "delete the file" is an Imperative. the reader is the addressee of an Imperative.
the Lexer splits a sentence into tokens. the Lexer gives a Form Tag to every token. the Lexer recognizes a Name and recognizes a quantity by the shape.
Markdown is the format of the documents. Markdown turns a dash into a bullet.
